title: Slot 11 relaxation plus diverse pool of 12
spec: On top of the penalty-energy L-BFGS-B relaxation of fresh starts (relax centres with radii fixed near 0.09, then SLSQP), grow the pool to 12 and reject new packings whose sorted radius vector is within 1e-3 L2 of any pool member. Crossover and perturbed starts pick parents uniformly from the pool. Combines the two best-replicated signals.

title: Annealed inflating penalty relaxation
spec: Replace the single penalty relaxation with a continuation: set target radii to 0.04, run L-BFGS-B on the squared overlap/wall penalty over centres only, then raise the targets by a factor of 1.15 per stage up to about 0.095 (6 stages, 30 iterations each), starting each stage from the previous centres. Then give the centres and the final target radii to SLSQP. This acts like a Lubachevsky-Stillinger compression and should give denser basins.

title: Remove-and-reinsert smallest circles into largest holes
spec: After each SLSQP result from a pool member, make a new start: take the best pool packing, delete the k=2 or 3 circles with the smallest radii, and re-place each at a random point chosen as the best of 200 random candidates, scored by the max distance to the nearest other circle edge (distance to the centres minus their radii, and the wall distance). Give each reinserted circle a radius of 0.02. Run SLSQP from this start. Use this for 30% of restarts in place of the crossover.

title: Joint centre and radius penalty optimisation with sum-of-radii reward
spec: Instead of fixed radii, run L-BFGS-B on variables (c, r) with energy -sum(r) + mu * (overlap^2 + wall^2), with mu increased through 10, 100, 1000 over three stages. Use the result as the SLSQP start. Gradients analytic and vectorised over pairs. Applies to fresh starts only.

title: Batch screening of many cheap relaxed starts by penalty energy
spec: Per restart round, generate 20 random starts, relax each with 30 L-BFGS-B steps of the penalty energy, and give SLSQP only the one with the lowest final energy (or the highest sum of radii after relaxation with radii as variables). This spends cheap compute to raise the quality of the SLSQP starts.

title: Mixed-size initial radii with hex-grid centres
spec: Replace random initialisation for non-crossover starts with a jittered hex-like grid. Use rows of 6,5,6,5,6,4 or similar totalling 32, with a row spacing of about 1/6 and a random jitter of sd 0.02. Set radii to uniform random values in [0.04,0.11]. Randomly permute which circles get large radii. This starts near the dense known structure rather than from uniform noise.

title: Penalty relaxation with random radius targets in a size-mixed band
spec: In the penalty-energy relaxation of fresh starts, draw per-circle target radii from a uniform [0.05, 0.13] distribution rescaled so that sum of pi r^2 is about 0.8, relax centres with L-BFGS-B, then start SLSQP with those radii times 0.8. This gives mixed-size basins consistent with the best known packings.

title: Region-swap crossover with penalty repair
spec: Replace the vertical-cut crossover by a random cut along a random line (angle uniform) between two pool parents. Take circles on one side from parent A and the other side from B, fix the count to 32 by removing the smallest overlappers or adding circles at random positions, run 30 steps of penalty-energy L-BFGS-B to remove overlap, then SLSQP. Keeps the pool of 5.

title: Penalty relaxation base plus pool 12 plus relocation (combined)
spec: Adopt the slot 11 base: fresh random starts are relaxed by L-BFGS-B on a smooth quadratic overlap/wall penalty energy (radii fixed at about 0.09) before SLSQP. Also use a pool of 12 with a 1e-3 L2 sorted-radius diversity filter. Replace the crossover with relocation: take a random pool member, remove one circle chosen with probability proportional to 1/radius, put it at a random position with a small radius, then run SLSQP. Keep the 70% pool-start / 30% fresh split.

title: Basin-aware restart allocation with stagnation reset
spec: Track the best sum over time. If the best has not improved for 25% of the elapsed budget, clear the pool except the best and do fresh penalty-relaxed starts only for the next 20% of the budget. Then resume the mixed strategy. This prevents the pool from collapsing into one basin.

title: Penalty-energy relaxation of fresh starts, with pool of 12 diverse
spec: Re-adopt slot 11: for fresh random starts, relax centres with L-BFGS-B on a smooth overlap-penalty energy (sum of squared overlaps of circles with fixed radii plus wall violations) before SLSQP. Additionally combine with slot 9: pool size 12, and skip a new packing if its sorted radius vector is within 1e-3 L2 of an existing pool member. Crossover and perturbation starts are drawn from the pool as before.

title: Wall-hugging bias in fresh centres
spec: Draw fresh centres from a mixture: 40% of circles sampled uniformly from a thin band within 0.1 of a random wall, the remaining 60% uniform in the square. Then apply the existing penalty relaxation and SLSQP. Good packings put many circles against the walls, with small ones filling corners.

title: Batch of cheap starts promoted by penalty energy
spec: Generate a batch of 40 random starts. Relax each with 30 L-BFGS-B steps on the overlap penalty energy, then compute the final energy plus -sum(r) score. Run full SLSQP only on the best 5 of the batch. Repeat the batch until the time is used, and feed the results into the pool as before. This spends little time on bad basins.

title: Adaptive restart allocation with stagnation reset
spec: Track the time of the last improvement of the best sum. If there has been no improvement for 6 s, clear the pool except for the best one, and switch to fresh penalty-relaxed starts only for the next 4 s so that the pool can refill with different basins. Otherwise, keep the current schedule.

title: Symmetric initialisation
spec: For half of the restarts, generate 16 random circles and mirror them about x=0.5 or the diagonal to give 32 as the starting point, then optimise without the symmetry constraint.

title: Swap radii between neighbours
spec: For 30% of restarts, take a random pool packing, choose two touching circles with different radii that are not neighbours of the same size class, swap their radii only (centres unchanged), shrink both by 20% for feasibility, then run SLSQP. Targets the discrete size-assignment structure of the optimum.

title: Mirror-symmetric half-packing starts
spec: For 25% of fresh starts, generate 16 random circles in the left half (x<0.5) with radius 0.06, and mirror them about x=0.5 to get 32 circles. Run SLSQP on the full 32-circle problem from this symmetric start; SLSQP will break symmetry if that is better. Other fresh starts stay random.

title: Squared-distance constraints with variable bounds
spec: Rewrite the SLSQP constraints as squared distance minus squared radius sum, which is smooth at zero distance. Express the wall and r>=0 constraints as bounds: r in [0, 0.5] and centres in [0, 1]. Keep the wall constraints c-r>=0 as linear constraints. This reduces the constraint count and gives a smoother Jacobian. Combine it with the slot 11 relaxation.

title: Size-mixed target radii in relaxation
spec: In the penalty pre-relaxation, give each circle a target radius drawn from a mixture: 6 circles at 0.13, 10 at 0.10 and 16 at 0.07, shuffled per start (rng). Penalise overlap against the sum of the two target radii. Initialise SLSQP radii with these targets scaled by 0.7. Optimal packings for this problem have mixed sizes, so this should give better basins.

title: Batch of cheap starts, then promote best by penalty energy
spec: Generate 8 fresh starts at a time. Relax each with L-BFGS-B on the overlap-penalty energy with radii fixed at 0.09. Rank them by the total sum of radii found from a quick LP on the relaxed centres. Run SLSQP only on the top 2 of the 8. This spends the time on promising basins.

title: Pool crossover on spatial region with local repair
spec: Replace the vertical-cut crossover with a random-angle line cut: pick a random direction and offset through the centre area, take circles on one side from parent A and the other side from parent B. Delete any circle in B's part whose centre lies within 0.5 of the sum of radii of an A circle, then refill to n with the largest-hole search. Give the child small radii (0.8x) before SLSQP so that it starts feasible.

title: Contact-graph-preserving restarts with radius reshuffle
spec: For a pool member, compute the touching pairs (gap < 1e-6). Pick a random circle with few contacts (a rattler or smaller one), and exchange its position and radius with a random circle of a different size, then run SLSQP. Complements the swap test by choosing based on contacts rather than uniformly. Apply to 30% of restarts after the pool has 3 members.

title: Wall-hugging biased fresh centres
spec: Draw fresh centres so that 40% of the circles are placed near the boundary: pick a wall, put the coordinate along the wall uniform, and put the perpendicular offset at 0.05+0.05*U. Draw the rest uniformly in the interior. Use initial radii of 0.06 for boundary circles and 0.1 for interior ones. The best packings known have many circles touching the walls.

title: Neighbour-only constraints with refresh
spec: In _solve_once, run SLSQP in rounds of at most 3. In each round include only pair constraints for pairs whose centre distance at the current x is under r_i+r_j+0.25, plus all wall constraints. After each round, check all pairs and stop if none is violated by more than 1e-9; otherwise recompute the set and warm start again. This cuts the constraint count from ~496 to ~150 and speeds each iteration. Use the freed time for more restarts.

title: Adopt penalty-relaxed fresh starts as base (replicated)
spec: In _solve_once's caller, for fresh starts (x0 None), draw uniform random centres, then run scipy L-BFGS-B (maxiter ~60) on a smooth energy: sum over pairs of max(0, 2*R - d)^2 plus wall violations max(0, R - c)^2 and max(0, c + R - 1)^2 with R=0.09, using analytic gradient via numpy vectorisation. Use relaxed centres with radii 0.05 as the SLSQP x0. Keep everything else as in the incumbent. This is the slot 11 setup that gave -2.9396 twice, so it is the single replicated improvement to adopt.

title: Swap-radius moves between neighbours in pool members
spec: For 30% of restarts, take a random pool packing and swap the radii of two circles of clearly different radius (ratio over 1.3) that are within 0.3 of each other, keeping centres. Run SLSQP from this start with maxiter 200. This explores permutations of big and small circles, a change that continuous local optimisation cannot reach. Do not apply large jitter.

title: Adaptive restart allocation by basin
spec: Track the sum of radii of each pool member and how often restarts from it improved the pool. Choose parents with probability proportional to exp((sum-best)/0.005). Choose the perturbation type (crossover, small jitter, fresh start) by a bandit rule using each type's past success rate. Use the slot 11 relaxation for the fresh starts.

title: Hot-start SLSQP with random radius-sum weights
spec: For 30% of restarts, take a pool member and run SLSQP with a perturbed objective -sum(w_i r_i), where w_i is uniform in [0.7, 1.3], for 80 iterations. Then switch to w=1 and run to convergence. The weights push the structure out of the current basin, and the final stage returns to the true objective.

title: Soft-radius p-norm objective continuation
spec: For each SLSQP start, first solve with the objective -sum(r^q) with q=0.7 for 60 iterations, which favours equalising radii and reaches a compact arrangement. Then switch to the true objective -sum(r) for the remaining iterations from that point. Use the same pair constraints. The first stage is a smoothing of the landscape.

title: Alternating LP-radii and centre-gradient polish
spec: After the restart loop, polish the best packing by a few rounds: fix radii and move centres a small step along the gradient that increases the minimum slack of active contacts (via scipy linprog on linearised constraints with a trust region 0.01 on the centre displacement and radius variables), then re-solve. This is a sequential LP (SLP) trust-region method with variables dx, dy, dr maximising sum dr subject to linearised non-overlap constraints, accepting steps that keep exact feasibility after repair. Use about 15% of the time.

title: Mirror-symmetric search with symmetric SLSQP
spec: For 40% of the time, optimise 16 free circles plus their mirror images across x=0.5, so the variables are 16 centres and radii. Constraints cover all 32 circles built from this. This halves the dimension and makes SLSQP much faster. Then desymmetrise the best result and polish it with a full 32-circle SLSQP for 200 iterations. Run the remaining time in the usual pool loop, seeding the pool with the polished results.
